technical_and_design_decisions: Custom modules will be built using Gradle, aligned with the CI infrastructure changes specified in U5.
The native WebSocket sink will leverage Spring Framework's built-in spring-websocket module to avoid external dependencies and ensure compatibility with Spring's messaging ecosystem.
Shared dependent jars will be stored in HDFS at the /xd/lib path with versioned subdirectories (e.g., /xd/lib/<jar-name>/<version>) to resolve classloader conflicts as recommended in U8.
CI infrastructure changes will be implemented on the existing Bamboo CI platform running on EC2, with no adoption of new CI tooling.
SonarQube violation notifications will be sent to code committers via email integrated with the existing Git version control system.
npm-cache will be deployed as a local sidecar service on CI nodes to cache npm dependencies, requiring no changes to existing build pipeline logic beyond cache configuration.
assumptions: An existing HDFS cluster is operational and accessible from both CI and production deployment environments, with no additional HDFS setup required.
The existing Bamboo CI server is already configured with EC2 agent provisioning capabilities for both Linux and Windows environments.
A SonarQube instance is already integrated with the version control system and existing CI pipeline, requiring only configuration changes for violation notifications.
Pre-built Windows installation packages for required integration test services (Redis, RabbitMQ) are available for deployment on Bamboo Windows agents.
Existing custom module test suites are compatible with distributed JVM test execution and maxParallelForks configuration.
The build pipeline includes steps that require npm dependencies (e.g., frontend asset compilation) that will benefit from the npm-cache implementation.
Existing Spring-based application code is compatible with Spring Framework 6.0+ and Java 17, as required by the specification.
